summary.intent: The user wanted to check the state of the someguy sidecar on staging, understand why it was underperforming compared to phase 18 metrics, and then fix a CI issue where Grafana dashboard provisioning was failing due to the instance not being ready post-deploy.
summary.outcome: Confirmed someguy is running and actively wired up (never actually disabled — likely reverted by a subsequent deploy). Implemented a Grafana instance readiness poll in the CI workflow and opened a PR on a `chore(ci):` branch.

repo: Someguy sidecar (ghcr.io/ipfs/someguy:v0.11.1) is deployed as part of docker-compose.staging.yml and is actively used via DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL=http://someguy:8190 in the API.
The TEE Worker still uses delegated-ipfs.dev — only the API routes through the self-hosted Someguy.
Someguy port 8190 is not published to the host; it is only accessible within the Docker network at 172.18.0.7.
The DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL is also hardcoded in the deploy-staging.yml workflow (line 397), which means server-side .env.staging changes get overwritten on each deploy.
This work is part of Phase 19: IPNS Resolution Improvement, documented under .planning/phases/19-ipns-resolution-improvement/.
Grafana Cloud free-tier instances sleep when idle and return 503 'Your instance is loading' when woken up — provisioning steps must wait for readiness before pushing dashboards.

code.finding: Fallback default for DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL is https://delegated-ipfs.dev if the env var is not set.
Code comment references DHT propagation via Someguy.
DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL=http://someguy:8190 is hardcoded here, meaning any manual .env.staging edits on the server are overwritten on each deploy.

workflow: When a 'disable' of a service isn't committed to git and baked into the deploy workflow, it will be silently re-enabled on the next deployment.
Grafana Cloud /api/health returns {"database":"ok"} with HTTP 200 when the instance is fully ready — use this as the readiness signal before provisioning.

friction: The someguy 'disable' was never persisted — either it was done via a direct server edit that was overwritten by a deploy, or it happened in a session that didn't produce a commit. This caused confusion about the current state.
Someguy port not being published to the host made it harder to test API endpoints directly; required exec-ing into the container or using another container on the same Docker network.
Grafana Cloud free-tier instance sleep behavior caused CI provisioning failures with a non-obvious 503 error.
open_items: Performance load tests against someguy are deferred until the latest staging deploy lands — user will trigger this manually.
Need to compare fresh someguy performance numbers against the phase 18 delegated-ipfs.dev baseline to decide whether to keep someguy or revert.
Consider whether DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL should be managed as a true secret/env rather than hardcoded in deploy-staging.yml, to allow persistent server-side overrides.
